weaknesses.title: IDOR — /rest/admin/application-configuration (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: The endpoint accesses administrative configuration data; if insufficient access controls are in place, unauthorized users might enumerate or access sensitive configurations.

weaknesses.title: CSRF — /rest/admin/application-configuration (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: Admin endpoints often lack CSRF protection; this GET request might perform state-changing actions or expose sensitive info if triggered by an attacker.

weaknesses.title: SSRF — /rest/admin/application-configuration (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: Admin config endpoints may fetch external resources (e.g., config files, service metadata); unsanitized inputs could lead to SSRF if backend makes requests based on user-accessible params.

weaknesses.title: Server Side Inclusion/Edge Side Inclusion Injection — /rest/admin/application-configuration (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: If the response includes dynamically generated content from server-side includes or edge-side includes, malicious expressions might be injected and executed.

weaknesses.title: Information Disclosure — /rest/admin/application-configuration (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: Administrative endpoints often expose sensitive configuration details; if access controls are weak, this could leak system credentials, paths, or deployment info.

weaknesses.title: AuthZ Bypass — /rest/admin/application-configuration (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: The admin path implies privileged access is expected; missing or flawed authorization checks might allow lower-privilege users to access configurations.

weaknesses.title: CRLF Injection — /rest/admin/application-configuration (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: If any part of the request influences HTTP headers or logging without sanitization, it might allow header injection or log poisoning.

weaknesses.title: Cache Poisoning — /rest/admin/application-configuration (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration)
weaknesses.rationale: If caching layers incorrectly handle this response based on varied inputs or headers, attackers might store malicious or sensitive responses in shared caches.

weaknesses.title: XSSI (Cross-Site Script Inclusion) — response body (GET /assets/i18n/en.json)
weaknesses.rationale: JSON files served statically can expose sensitive data to malicious sites if not properly configured with CORS or wrapped in a function.

weaknesses.title: Client-Side Path Traversal — path segment in URL (GET /assets/i18n/en.json)

weaknesses.title: SSRF (Server Side Request Forgery) — unknown dynamic parameter (GET /assets/i18n/en.json)

weaknesses.title: Open Redirect — Host header or unseen parameters (GET /assets/i18n/en.json)
weaknesses.rationale: Servers sometimes reflect Host headers or hidden parameters in redirect locations, allowing attackers to redirect users to malicious sites.

weaknesses.title: Cache Poisoning — Host header or query string (GET /assets/i18n/en.json)
weaknesses.rationale: If the application caches responses based on host or query parameters without proper validation, it might serve poisoned content to other users.

weaknesses.title: File Inclusion (Local/Remote) — path interpretation (GET /assets/i18n/en.json)
weaknesses.rationale: The server might interpret the path as a file reference and include unintended local or remote files if path traversal or null byte injection is possible.

weaknesses.title: Parameter Pollution — query parameters (`EIO`, `transport`, `t`, GET /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: Duplicate or maliciously crafted parameters could interfere with socket handshake or routing logic.

weaknesses.title: SSRF — query parameter `transport` (GET /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: If `transport` influences internal resource fetching (e.g., polling endpoints), it may be abused to access unintended internal services.

weaknesses.title: WebSockets Misconfiguration — upgrade path from polling (`transport=polling`, GET /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: Initial polling requests may lead to WebSocket upgrades; injecting unexpected values could expose improper message handling or authentication bypasses.

weaknesses.title: XSS — query parameter `t` (GET /socket.io/)

weaknesses.title: Cache Deception — query parameters (`EIO`, `transport`, `t`, GET /socket.io/)

weaknesses.title: CRLF Injection — query parameters (`EIO`, `transport`, `t`, GET /socket.io/)

weaknesses.title: SSRF — internal service probing (GET /rest/admin/application-version)

weaknesses.title: Information Disclosure — verbose version fingerprinting (GET /rest/admin/application-version)

weaknesses.title: Authentication Bypass — unauthenticated admin access (GET /rest/admin/application-version)

weaknesses.title: CORS Misconfiguration — cross-origin version theft (GET /rest/admin/application-version)

These areas merit immediate targeted review given their potential critical impact if exploitable (CVSS >7). Untested issues highlight broader architectural weaknesses potentially allowing unauthorized data exposure, cache poisoning, and injection vectors. Prioritize validating high-risk entrypoints with active testing tools and address proven exposures immediately—especially around identity management, server-side request handling and cross-origin protections. Confidence varies widely; proven findings demand urgent patching while others require further scrutiny to confirm viability.
